messages:
Sam: heads-up — CumulusHealth reporting p99 spikes on /v1/embeddings since ~21:00 UTC yesterday. Customer seeing 10–12s tail latencies and intermittent 502s. Trace id included in examples below: tx/0a1b2c. They want an urgent mitigation.

Lukas: can you drop one exact curl + headers + model name and a couple of raw timings? also which tenant id?

Sam: example request (api key redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Trace-Id: tx/0a1b2c" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["...bulk batch..."],"tenant_id":"cum-88"}'
```
raw response samples we collected from the customer: 120ms, 258ms, 10.4s, 11.2s (10s+ correspond to 502 or timeout followed by retry).

Priya: looking at traces (tx/0a1b2c) — majority are KV cache misses and a lot of shard rebalances on embed worker pool embed-e4. There's one heavy bulk job from tenant cum-88 that started ~20:50 and seems to be thrashing the KV cache and causing continuous long tail ops. @Jordan can you check embed pool queue depth and per-tenant share?

Jordan: infra findings — embed-pool-e4 queue spiked. p95 enqueue->start ~1.2s, p99 ~9.8s during the window. Tenant cum-88 accounts for ~68% of active tasks in the backlog. We do have fairness but this workload exceeded the burst window and caused head-of-line delays. Ops-bot alert posted: "embed-queue-e4 backlog high" (alert id alert-5521).

ops-bot: ALERT alert-5521 — embed-queue-e4 backlog > 700 tasks for 10m. https://internal.redwood/alerts/alert-5521

Priya: immediate mitigation options (short-term):
1) soft per-tenant throttle for cum-88 (limit to 8–12 RPS) for 30m to let backlog drain.
2) create a temporary reservation (priority seats) on embed-e4 if customer has reserved capacity or we can offer a 2-slot emergency reservation.
3) route cum-88 to embed-small-q4 (quantized smaller model) as an automatic fallback for bulk jobs.
4) ask customer to pause their bulk embedding job while we drain queues.

Lukas: I can apply the soft throttle + reservation now. commands I'm running: 
```
# soft per-tenant throttle
rictl tenants rate-limit --tenant cum-88 --rps 10 --duration 30m

# temporary reservation (2 slots) on embed-e4
rictl reservation create --tenant cum-88 --pool embed-e4 --slots 2 --duration 2h --reason "emergency backpressure"
```

Sam: I'll ask CumulusHealth to pause the job and accept fallback to embed-small-q4 for any urgent requests. Pinged them in the support ticket, copying the trace id and the sample logs.

Jordan: applied throttle and created reservation. reservation id res/7721. Post-change telemetry: queue dropped from 820 -> 140 over 18 minutes; p99 enqueue->start reduced to 1.1s. Incident created: 2026-IR-4567. Monitoring graphs: https://internal.redwood/mon/embed-e4?incident=2026-IR-4567

Priya: medium-term action items:
- add auto-detect to soft-throttle when a tenant is >60% of queue for 3m (GH: redwood/infra#8451).
- add a policy to prefer fallback to quantized models for large batch embeds if tenant flagged as "bulk-job".
- postmortem to include customer guidance for bulk-ingest (rate limits / reservations).

Sam: CumulusHealth replied: "Paused the job and accepted fallback, thanks — we'll coordinate to retry with reservations next week." :white_check_mark:

Lukas: closing the emergency work. Will follow up with CS to confirm billing/reservation offer.

Priya: leaving GH issue and playbook updates for oncall. Marking incident as mitigated; will keep monitoring for 2h.

Jordan: note: retention logs for KV eviction window saved under /logs/incidents/2026-IR-4567/kv-evict.log for postmortem.

Sam: thx everyone — I'll update the customer thread and schedule a handoff with Solutions to discuss reserved capacity options.
